findings.text: The three cases prove the store is one value, but none proves the reader takes it once. reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py:77 now reads `pair = _MOUNTS_MEMO.pair` into a local, and the docstring at :73-75 states that property as the reason the race is closed. The probe at tests/test_a_roadmap_read_answers_from_its_snapshot.py:711-734 fires only from `__setattr__`, so it observes states between stores and never a pair of reads inside remembered_mounts. A regression that kept the one-value store and re-read the global twice, e.g. `if _MOUNTS_MEMO.pair is not None and _MOUNTS_MEMO.pair[0] == stamp: return _MOUNTS_MEMO.pair[1]`, would leave test_a_reader_never_sees_a_stamp_beside_mounts_from_another_store green while reopening the mixed pair it exists to prevent. The store half of the fix is well guarded; the read half is asserted only by inspection.

The dispatch's FENCE - SCOPE (prompt.txt:69-76) lists reckon/serve.py, reckon/mcp.py, reckon/_store.py, the test module, the evidence fragment and the figure, and again omits reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py, which the gained commit ef5407e63 writes. Plan section 50 at docs/plans/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline.html:318 names reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py in its write paths explicitly, so the write is plan-authorized and the fence is the defective artefact rather than the worker's scope. Recorded because the third consecutive dispatch of this node carries the same omission, so a worker who obeyed the fence literally would be unable to answer any finding in the module the section assigns it.
